page: Microsoft Azure E104i_v5 is an isolated, x86_64 architecture server belonging to the EIv5 family. It features 104 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 52 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores running at 2.8 GHz, with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 6.46 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 100,833.46 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,815.0, both placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also strong, showing a read-only large block bandwidth of 334.7 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2,937.28. Cryptographic operations are highly efficient, with the PassMark CPU encryption test reaching the top 10% tier at 93,156.86. However, single-core performance is average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,708.0.

The high density of dedicated vCPUs and memory provides a consolidated resource profile, offering qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that would otherwise require multiple smaller instances, though the lack of local storage requires factoring in external storage costs. While the server excels at multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, database operations, and Redis SET operations, it exhibits limitations in large-scale AI workloads. Large model LLM text generation is weak, processing only 2.67 tokens per second. Given the high memory capacity and dedicated compute resources, this server is suited for memory-intensive enterprise databases, large-scale web serving, and multi-threaded data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E104i_v5 is an isolated, memory-optimized server in the EIv5 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor. It features 104 dedicated vCPUs across 52 physical cores, 672.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 79,491.91 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 470.08 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is in the top 10% tier, though single-core benchmarks and large-scale LLM text generation are average to weak. This configuration is suited for memory-intensive databases, enterprise web serving, and concurrent software compilation.
